meta.title: Ch 15: Startup Finance — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 15 (Startup Finance).

questions.q: The scorecard method of startup valuation differs from the Berkus method by:
o: Adjusting a pre-money benchmark for qualitative factors (team, market size, competition, stage)
questions.why: Scorecard: benchmark average pre-money of similar startups, then apply weighted factor comparisons (team, product, market, competition, funding). Berkus: caps each value driver at a fixed dollar range — both are early-stage heuristics in the new syllabus.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — new-syllabus chapter methods are high-visibility in MCQs AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: No cash flows yet? Grade the journey, cap the dream.

questions.q: Compared with VCs, angel investors typically:
o: Provide early-stage capital, own judgement, smaller tickets, often less formal governance
questions.why: Angels: own money, pre-seed/seed, judgement-based, network mentoring; VCs: institutional funds, diligence, stages A+, board seats.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — stage-and-style mapping of investors AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Angels open the door; VCs widen the hallway and watch the exits.

questions.q: Investor buys 20% for Rs 8 crore in a round: the post-money and pre-money valuations are:
questions.why: Post = 8/0.20 = 40 crore; pre = 40 − 8 = 32. The flip is the trap; dilution: founder 100%→80%.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the pre/post subtraction trap AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Post-money is the pie with the new flour in it; pre is what you had before.

questions.q: A down-round (lower valuation than prior) typically triggers:
questions.why: Pre-existing investors invoke full-ratchet/weighted-average anti-dilution — founders/employees absorb the share-count effect.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — term-sheet vocabulary from the startup chapter Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: A down round opens old contracts before it closes the round.

questions.q: Monthly net cash burn Rs 2 crore with Rs 30 crore raised and Rs 4 crore already spent: runway ≈
questions.why: Cash left 26 ÷ 2 = 13 months — the arithmetic of startup finance; note pre-money runway is dilution's clock.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — runway arithmetic as a guaranteed 1-marker Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Runway is simple maths with hard consequences; the plane doesn't negotiate with months.

questions.q: A round raises Rs 15 crore at Rs 40 crore pre-money. The investor's fresh equity share:
questions.why: Post-money = 40 + 15 = 55 crore, so the investor share = 15/55 = 27.3% — dividing by PRE-money (which gives 37.5%) is the classic miss.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the pre/post division trap defines startup-round arithmetic AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: New % = investment ÷ post-money; founder % diluted accordingly.

questions.q: Benchmark pre-money for the region/sector Rs 40 crore. A startup scores 1.3× on team, 0.9× market, 1.1× competition and 1.0× others (equal weights). The scorecard-method pre-money ≈
questions.why: Average factor = 1.08 ⇒ value ≈ 43.0 crore — the method's essence: weighted factor ratios applied to a benchmark, NOT cash-flow based.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the new-syllabus method applied with tiny math — high-alert first-attempt material Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Weighted factor adjustment on a benchmark pre-money.

questions.q: A 'liquidation preference 1x participating' for an investor means on a downside sale they get:|
o: Their ordinary share of proceeds only
The lower of invested amount or ordinary proceeds, then share again (double dip)
questions.why: Preference = be paid first up to (1x = invested) before common; participating then also rides the residual pro-rata; anti-dilution and ratchets are different protections — know which clause does what.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — preference is the first slice; participation takes a second helping AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: First the guarantee, then the crowd — a participating preferred eats twice.

questions.q: Most defensible early-stage valuation practice for a 2-year-old SaaS is:
o: Berkus/stage-based plus comparable-transactions triangulation with explicit milestones
questions.why: No reliable cash flows → method shifts to stage/asset-building methods (Berkus, scorecard) and recent comparable rounds, with the narrative of de-risked milestones; DCF is accepted for a 10-year plan but must be caveated with scenario bands.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — pre-cashflow: price the de-risking, not the forecast AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: You can't DCF a dream — you can list what makes it less of one.

questions.q: ESOPs to employees are expensed under Ind AS 102 as:
o: Fair value of options at grant date amortised over the vesting period
questions.why: Grant-date fair value spread over vesting period into P&L with credit to employee stock options/outstanding equity reserve (equity-settled); market conditions in the grant fair value, non-market vesting conditions in the vesting estimate — re-measurement stops at grant date for equity-settled plans.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — measured at grant, charged over vesting, never re-priced after Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: The cost is fixed the day the promise is made; the ledger only spreads it.

questions.q: Monthly burn 40 lakh, cash in bank 4 crore: runway is:
questions.why: Runway = cash ÷ net burn (outflows minus inflows) = 400/40 = 10 months; founders must quote post-burn adjustments (hiring plan) and next-milestone timing against it — mechanical math, judgment caveat.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — runway ends when either the money or the story does Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Cash is the tank; burn is the meter; the milestone is the airport.
